entry.title: File Hover Info 1.1.1
entry.content:
File Hover Info

Rest the cursor on a file, folder, drive or shortcut — on the desktop or in a File Explorer window — and a card appears with the details you choose: size, folder size, free space on drives, creation / modification / access dates, attributes, image dimensions, media duration, file version, shortcut target, folder contents and location.

The card follows the Windows display language (English, Italian, Spanish, French, German and Portuguese are included; other languages fall back to English), or you can pick one.

Everything is configurable: which fields to show, date style (absolute, relative or both), theme (follow Windows, dark, light or fully custom colors), solid / acrylic / blur background, accent color and bar, corner radius, shadow, fade-in, font, size, icon or thumbnail.

Windows' own popup

By default the mod hides Windows' built-in hover popup, so only the card is shown. This only affects Explorer while the mod is running: the Windows setting itself is not changed, and the popup comes back as soon as the option or the mod is turned off. The option also hides the small tooltip Windows shows for desktop icon names that are cut off, since the card shows the full name anyway.

Folder size

Folder sizes are summed on a background thread, so Explorer is never blocked. The card shows "Calculating…" and updates when the total is ready. The calculation stops as soon as the cursor moves away, and after the time limit set in the options (the card then shows a partial total). Drives show their free space instead of being scanned.

Notes

  • Acrylic and blur use an undocumented Windows API; on some builds the blur may not follow the rounded corners.
  • Items are matched by their displayed name. If two items in the same folder show the same name (e.g. photo.jpg and photo.png with extensions hidden), the first one is shown.
  • Pages that aren't classic folder views (Home, Gallery) are not supported.

entry.title: Real-time Cast Shadow Wallpaper 1.0.3
entry.content:
Real-time Cast Shadow Wallpaper

Turns the desktop into a lit surface: a light source moves over your wallpaper and every visible window casts a projected shadow on it, updated in real time as you move, resize and drag windows.

Watch the full-quality video

Features

  • Light motion: follow the mouse, wander randomly, orbit the screen, sweep across it like the sun, follow the real time of day, or stay fixed.
  • Light presets: warm lamp, daylight, flickering candle, moonlight, neon, or fully custom color, intensity, radius and height.
  • Shadow presets: crisp, soft, diffuse, long (dramatic), subtle, or custom opacity, softness and length.
  • Anchored shadows: the shadow stays attached to the window base and stretches away from the light, with a sharp contact edge and a soft tail.
  • Contact shadow: a soft darkening right around each window that grounds it on the desktop, independent of the light.
  • Shadow color: neutral, cool, warm or violet shadows.
  • Shadows on other windows (optional): windows also shade the applications below them, following the real window stacking order.
  • Background: your current Windows wallpaper (per monitor, slideshows included), a custom image, or a plain dark surface; optional vignette.
  • Multi-monitor support, pause on fullscreen apps, smooth tracking while dragging windows.

Light motion

| Motion | Behavior | |---|---| | Follow the mouse | The light follows the cursor across all monitors. | | Wander | Smooth random paths, independent on each monitor. | | Orbit | A slow elliptical orbit around the center of each monitor. | | Sun arc | Rises on the left, crosses the top, sets on the right, then repeats. Shadows are long and the light warm near the horizon. | | Time of day | Like the sun arc, but driven by your clock: sunrise at 6:00, noon at the top, sunset at 20:00, then a dim moonlight arc at night. | | Fixed point | Pinned to a position in % of the monitor; values below 0 or above 100 place it off-screen for long, raking shadows. |

"Speed" applies to wander, orbit and sun arc.

Presets

Choosing a light or shadow preset overrides the matching custom values; pick "Custom" to use your own. Shadow presets express length relative to the light height, so they look consistent with every light preset.

Notes

  • Windows are approximated as rounded rectangles with a common virtual height: shadows don't follow transparency or irregular window shapes.
  • Shadows are drawn on the wallpaper behind the desktop icons. Shadows on other windows use a click-through overlay that never covers the window casting them; the taskbar, menus and tooltips are left untouched. This option adds some CPU/GPU load.
  • Rendering uses OpenGL (GLSL 1.20). On current Windows 11 desktops, frames are only redrawn when the light, the windows or the background change, so a still desktop costs almost nothing (the flickering candle redraws continuously). On older desktop layouts every frame is drawn, up to the FPS limit.
  • Rendering pauses while the session is locked, the display is off, or every monitor shows a fullscreen app. If the desktop isn't ready yet (at sign-in, or while Explorer restarts), the mod waits and attaches when it appears.
  • The Windows wallpaper setting is never modified, Explorer's own windows are never reordered, and nothing is written to the registry. Disabling the mod removes everything it created.
  • Disable other animated-wallpaper mods while using this one.

entry.title: Lock Screen Date and Time Format 1.0
entry.content:
Lock Screen Date and Time Format

Changes how the Windows lock screen shows the time and the date. The mod only changes the text of the clock and the date. Fonts, sizes, colors and positions are not touched (see Styling below).

Example (Windows default on the left, this mod on the right):

| Before | After | |--------|-------| | | |

The clock keeps updating on its own, and choosing the "Windows default" options restores the original text.

Settings

Clock

  • Clock layout

  • Windows default: the clock is left alone.

  • Vertical: hours, minutes (and seconds) each on their own line, no separator.

  • Horizontal with custom separator: everything on one line, joined by the separator below.

  • Line spacing (% of font size): distance between the lines of a vertical clock, as a percentage of the clock font size. Lower is tighter, higher is looser, 0 keeps the font's default. It only has an effect when the clock has more than one line. About 80 to 85 is a good starting point.

  • Separator (horizontal layout): the text placed between hours, minutes and seconds. It is plain text, so a colon, a dot, a dash, a space, or even an emoji all work.

    Example with an emoji as the separator:

  • Hour format: follow the Windows short time format (the one the lock screen shows), or force 24-hour or 12-hour.

  • Leading zero on hours: show 09 or 9.

  • Show seconds: also show the seconds (15:19:42). The clock then updates every second instead of once a minute. With the vertical layout this gives three lines, so you will probably want a smaller font.

  • AM/PM position (12-hour only): beside the last unit shown, on its own line below, or hidden.

Digits are always shown as 0-9, whatever the Windows language is.

Note: the line spacing, separator, hour format, leading zero, show seconds and AM/PM options only take effect when Clock layout is Vertical or Horizontal. With Windows default the clock is left completely alone.

Date

  • Date format: choose one of the presets (for example Fri, 16 Oct, Fri 16 Oct 26, 16-10-2026, 16/10/2026), keep the Windows default, or choose Custom.
  • Custom date pattern: only used when the format is Custom. Supported letters: d / dd (day), ddd / dddd (weekday name), M / MM (month number), MMM / MMMM (month name), yy / yyyy (year). Literal text goes in single quotes, for example dddd 'the' d.

Weekday and month names come from your Windows regional format, so they follow that language.

Notes on the 12-hour format

AM/PM is placed after the last unit shown: the minutes, or the seconds when Show seconds is on. The examples below assume seconds are off:

  • Vertical layout, AM/PM beside the minutes: hours on the first line, minutes and AM/PM on the second line (03 / 24 PM).
  • Vertical layout, AM/PM below: three lines (03 / 24 / PM).
  • Horizontal layout, AM/PM beside the minutes: everything on one line (03:24 PM). With a very large clock font the line can be wider than the space it has, and PM may wrap onto a second line. Use a smaller font, or set AM/PM to hidden, if that bothers you.
  • AM/PM hidden: only the hours and minutes are shown.

Styling

This mod does not change fonts, sizes, colors or positions. For that, use the Windows 11 Start Menu Styler mod with LockApp.exe added to its process inclusion list. For example:

- target: StackPanel#TimePanel > TextBlock#Time
  styles:
    - FontSize=350
    - FontWeight=Bold
- target: TextBlock#Date
  styles:
    - FontSize=28

Example with this mod and the Styler together:

Making the clock font bigger usually moves the clock; adjust a TranslateTransform in the Styler if it ends up off-center.

Lock the screen with Win+L to see the result. Changes in the settings apply right away while the lock screen is showing.

How it works

The lock screen (LockApp.exe) draws the time and the date in XAML TextBlock elements named Time and Date. This mod finds them, builds the text itself from the system clock according to your settings, and writes it back whenever Windows updates them. Unloading the mod puts Windows' own text back.

The width of the clock is also kept constant, so the date underneath does not move sideways when the clock text gets wider or narrower (for example when the seconds change, or when AM switches to PM). This is skipped when the clock takes up almost the whole width of the screen, because there is no room left for it to move and forcing a width could get it cut off.

Known limitations

  • The mod relies on the internal element names Time and Date in LockApp.exe. If a future Windows update renames them, the mod will stop finding them.
  • Digits are always Latin (0-9). Showing the digits of your own language is not supported yet.
  • The AM/PM text cannot be made smaller than the clock yet.
  • Most fonts have digits of different widths, so with Show seconds on, the digits inside the clock can shift slightly every second. The date and the position of the clock stay where they are, except when the clock takes up almost the whole width of the screen. Pick a font with equal-width digits in the Styler if that bothers you.
  • Tested on Windows 11 25H2 (build 26200.9457). Other versions are untested.

Troubleshooting

If nothing happens, open the Windhawk log for this mod and lock the screen with Win+L. You should see Hook installed on UI thread, Clock format attached and Date format attached.

entry.title: Windows 11 Taskbar Drag and Lock 1.0.0
entry.content:
Bring back the Windows 10 ability to drag the taskbar to left, top, right and bottom, and lock it with the "Lock Taskbar" item in the taskbar context menu. The lock remembered from the context menu prevents accidental drags.

Requires the native Windows 11 taskbar position setting (Windows 11 26H2, build 26300+).

The taskbar is moved through the same native setting as Windows Settings, so a drag is equivalent to changing the position in Settings: it applies immediately, without restarting Explorer, and it persists after the mod is disabled. The setting is stored as a DWORD value named TaskbarLocation under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced, and can be changed back in Settings at any time. The taskbar moves between screen edges only; it cannot be dragged to another monitor.

Not compatible with mods that force a fixed taskbar position, such as Taskbar on top or Vertical Taskbar.

Based on the taskbar-empty-space-clicks mod by m1lhaus (input handling, GPL-3.0), the Taskbar Move mod by Asteski (native position setting), the Taskbar Restart Explorer mod by Mgrmjp (context menu injection), and the Taskbar Labels mod by m417z (taskbar-thread dispatch helpers).

entry.title: Taskbar Smoke 1.2.0
entry.content:
Taskbar Smoke

Draws a transparent, click-through overlay with animated dark smoke around the Windows 11 taskbar.

  • Five smoke styles: a real-time fluid simulation (the smoke rises, swirls and drifts over the edge), a classic layered texture smoke, and three tuned variants of the fluid smoke.
  • Reacts to the mouse: moving the cursor across the taskbar pushes the smoke aside; it flows back on its own.
  • Eight colors (violet, pink, light blue, ice blue, green, gold, orange, red), plus the Windows accent color or a slow rainbow cycle. An optional second color blends along each pill, from left to right.
  • Opacity in seven steps (17% to 150%), density, speed, tone (dark smoke or light glow), halo thickness and mouse reach.
  • Optional small dark clouds slowly rising from the taskbar.
  • Follows auto-hide, hides in fullscreen apps, settings apply instantly.

Works best with a dark, pill-shaped taskbar theme (e.g. Windows 11 Taskbar Styler); the smoke follows the taskbar's button groups. Runs in its own process (tool mod), Explorer is not modified.

Limitations: primary taskbar only, designed for a bottom-docked taskbar.

entry.title: Taskbar Open Window Underline 1.0
entry.content:
Taskbar Open Window Underline

Underlines the label of every Windows 11 taskbar button that has a window currently shown on the desktop. Buttons whose windows are all minimized keep a plain label, so you can tell at a glance which apps actually have something open in front of you.

Whole label

First letter only

Requirements:

  • Windows 11 with the XAML taskbar (22H2 or newer).
  • Taskbar labels must be visible: Settings → Personalization → Taskbar → Taskbar behaviors → "Combine taskbar buttons and hide labels" set to Never (or When taskbar is full). The "Show labels, combine taskbar buttons" mode of the Taskbar Labels mod is supported as well; a combined group is underlined when any (or, optionally, every) one of its windows is shown.

How it works:

  • The taskbar's buttons live in an ItemsRepeater; each button's item is its view model (TaskListWindowViewModel for one window, TaskListGroupViewModel for a group), and the view model knows its windows through the shell's TaskItem / TaskGroup objects. The mod resolves every button's windows that way and judges them with IsIconic (plus DWM cloaking for windows on other virtual desktops). Win+D counts as minimized.
  • A WinEvent hook (minimize / restore / show / hide / cloak, and foreground or title changes when a setting needs them) invalidates the buttons; events are coalesced and every button is re-evaluated on the taskbar thread, on every taskbar.
  • The underline is the native TextBlock underline, so it follows the text color, trimming and theme. It can cover the whole label or just its first letter. It is removed when the mod is disabled.
  • On builds where the view-model symbols can't be resolved, the mod falls back to matching label text against window titles, which is exact for "Never combine" but blind to combined groups.

entry.title: Custom Cached Context Menu 1.1.0
entry.content:
Added

  • Top action bar (opt-in): Cut, Copy, Paste, Rename and Delete as an icon bar on the side of the menu nearest the cursor, like the Windows 11 menu. Unavailable actions are hidden from the bar.
  • Paste into a single right-clicked folder, like the Windows 11 menu.

Fixed

  • Middle-clicking a folder no longer fails to open it in a new tab (invocation-only menu builds are no longer deferred).
  • The icon cache no longer runs its destructor at process exit.
  • Items that report SFGAO_FOLDER but are not directories (for example .zip files) no longer get the folder menu and its Paste.
  • Actions no longer wait for the shell menu: Open, Cut, Copy, Delete, Properties and Set as desktop background are dispatched directly, and registered extension verbs (Share, Print, Open in Terminal and others) run through the shell's association lookup, so clicking an action starts it immediately instead of after a short pause with a busy cursor. The shell menu is only populated for items that exist only inside it.
  • The menu disappears immediately when an action is chosen instead of playing the closing animation, so nothing lingers on screen while a modal dialog (Properties, the delete confirmation) is up.
  • Cut and Copy run the file view's own command when the view owns the keyboard (guarded so the keys can never land in another window), keeping the cut dimming, the shell clipboard data object and undo exactly like the native menu; otherwise they write the clipboard directly. Paste drops the clipboard object on the target folder's drop target — the shell's own paste path — so collision naming, undo and virtual clipboard items match, including for a right-clicked folder and the navigation tree.
  • Hover highlights track the mouse immediately during fast sweeps: interactive repaints no longer wait for vsync, and a burst of mouse moves paints only the final hover position.
  • Windows items that are not moved into the submenu no longer jump to the top of background menus; they stay with the other extras above the "More options" entry.

Changed

  • Theme names in the settings now match the bundled theme previews.
  • Default padding tightened to 4; existing configs and theme files are migrated when they still carry the old default (schema v9). Right-aligned content now mirrors the icon's left inset.
  • The "Windows items to move" default list uses language-independent verbs where they exist instead of English labels (labels still work as a fallback); commands whose verb is a GUID accept friendly aliases (openterminal, editwithphotos, editwithpaint, editwithnotepad), and Windows' modern commands are no longer treated as third-party handlers.

entry.title: Caption Buttons Customizer 1.0
entry.content:
Caption Buttons Customizer

Moves the caption buttons (minimize, maximize, close) to the left side of the title bar and repositions the window icon and title to match. It can also draw macOS-style traffic lights (red / yellow / green circles) or your own button images.

It works by hooking internal functions of the Desktop Window Manager (dwm.exe / uDWM.dll), so it affects every standard Windows window.

Setup

dwm.exe is a critical system process, so Windhawk does not inject into it by default. To use this mod, add dwm.exe to the process inclusion list: Windhawk Settings > Advanced settings > More advanced settings > Process inclusion list. Without it, only the explorer.exe part of the mod loads and the caption buttons will not move.

Features & Preview

Caption Buttons

Buttons on the left, with a left margin and three order presets: close / minimize / maximize (macOS), close / maximize / minimize, minimize / maximize / close.

Move caption buttons to the left = on

Turn on Move caption buttons to the left to move the buttons to the left side of the title bar. When it is off, they stay in their default place on the right.

| Before | After | |---------|---------| | | |

Button order

Pick one of three presets in the Button order setting. The order is counted from the left edge of the window.

| Close, minimize, maximize | Close, maximize, minimize | Minimize, maximize, close | |---------------------------|---------------------------|---------------------------| | | | |

Show the close button on dialogs

Windows with only a close button (message boxes, About windows, Properties dialogs) and very narrow windows are handled. The close button of dialogs can be hidden with Show the close button on dialogs, and their icon and title can have their own alignment.

| Dialog On | Dialog Off | |--------|-------| | | |

Caption Button Style

Three button styles are available in Caption button style: the default Windows glyphs (default), macOS circles in colors you choose (with the x, - and + symbols on hover), or your own images (png, jpg or bmp).

| macOS style (circles) | Custom images | Windows default | |-----------------------|---------------|-----------------| | | | |

Custom button images

  1. Set Caption button style to Custom images. (With the macOS style, the image settings are ignored and the circles stay as they are.)
  2. Set Icon folder (or the path of each button image) to any folder you can read, for example C:\Users\You\Pictures\ButtonIcons.
  3. Name the files minimize, restore, maximize, close (+ .png, .jpg, .jpeg or .bmp).
  4. Optional state variants: close_hover (mouse is over the button), close_pressed (button is being clicked) and close_disabled (button is greyed out). Same for the other buttons. If a variant is missing, the base image is used (darkened for pressed). The four base images are enough.
  5. Images are scaled down to fit the button slot (about 12 px at 100% DPI) and keep their own shape. They are not cut into a circle, so square images stay square. Use transparent PNGs and simple designs.
  6. A button without an image keeps its circle.

dwm.exe runs under its own account and usually cannot read your profile folders. To get around that, the part of the mod running inside explorer.exe (which can read your folders) decodes your images, shrinks them to at most 64 px, and hands the pixels to dwm.exe through the mod's own storage in Windhawk. No image files are copied anywhere, and dwm.exe never opens or decodes an image file.

If a changed image doesn't show up right away, move the mouse over a title bar button.

Icon and title text

Flexible icon and title layout: next to the buttons, centered on the window, or right-aligned; icon on either side of the title, far left or far right; hide the icon, the title, or both.

Icon and title alignment

Icon and title alignment decides where the icon and title sit in the title bar. Left puts them right after the buttons, Center puts them in the middle of the window, and Right puts them at the right edge.

| Left | Center | Right | |------|--------|-------| | | | |

Icon Position

Icon position decides where the window icon goes. Left or right of the title keeps the icon attached to the title, while far left or far right pins the icon to that edge.

To pin the icon to the left edge of the window instead of right after the buttons, turn off Move caption buttons to the left. To pin it to the right edge, turn that option on (with it off, a far right icon sits next to the buttons on the right instead). For the best look with an icon pinned to a corner, set Icon and title alignment to Center.

| Left of the title | Right of the title | |-------------------|--------------------| | | | | Far left | Far right | | | |

Hide window icon and title

Use Hide window icon and title to hide only the icon, only the title, or both.

| Hide icon only | Hide title only | Hide both | |----------------|-----------------|-----------| | | | |

Icon responds to click and double-click

By default, Windows treats the window icon as a button: clicking it opens the window menu (Restore, Move, Size, Minimize, Maximize and Close), and double-clicking it closes the window.

This can get in the way when Icon and title alignment is set to Center, because the icon then sits in the middle of the title bar, where it's easy to double-click by accident and close the window. Turn off Icon responds to click and double-click to prevent that. The icon then behaves like an empty part of the title bar: you can drag the window by it, and double-clicking it maximizes or restores the window.

File Explorer

The tab bar of File Explorer covers the left part of the title bar and blocks the buttons. The mod (running inside explorer.exe) makes the buttons clickable again, but the tabs themselves must be shifted with a separate mod. | File Explorer caption buttons on the right (default) | File Explorer caption buttons on the left | |------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------| | | |

Notes:

  • File Explorer caption buttons on the right (default): CabinetWClass is in Excluded window classes by default, so File Explorer keeps the default Windows layout. To keep this, leave it in the list.
  • File Explorer caption buttons on the left: Remove CabinetWClass from Excluded window classes, then turn on Make caption buttons clickable in File Explorer so the buttons can be clicked. The tabs stay where they are and still visually overlap the buttons, so shift them with the Windows 11 File Explorer Styler mod by m417z (target FileExplorerExtensions.FileExplorerTabControl, style Margin=187,0,0,0; this value works well for me, so adjust it to taste).
  • Alternatively, set Shift tab bar and toolbar (px) in File Explorer tabs (for example 145) to move the whole tab bar and toolbar to the right of the buttons instead of using Styler. This also moves the navigation arrows, address bar and search box.

Excluded apps

Apps that draw their own tabs in the title bar can conflict with buttons on the left. Add their executable names to Excluded apps (or their window class names to Excluded window classes) and every window of those apps keeps the default Windows layout.

By default Excluded apps contains notepad.exe, taskmgr.exe and WindowsTerminal.exe. The icon and title of Task Manager overlap the buttons, and the tabs of Notepad and Windows Terminal overlap the buttons when they are on the left. To see how these apps look with the buttons on the left, remove them from the list. Fixing them properly is planned for later, when time allows.

CabinetWClass (File Explorer) is in Excluded window classes by default, see the File Explorer section above.

Files created by the mod

None. Custom images are passed to dwm.exe through Windhawk's mod storage, and with Write debug log on (off by default) the mod writes detailed messages to the Windhawk log output instead of files. Logs can contain folder paths (including your Windows user name), so check them before sharing.

Important notes

  • When you use the macOS or custom style, drawing the glyphs rewrites a bitmap that DWM shares between all windows. The original glyphs come back only after dwm.exe restarts: sign out and in, run taskkill /f /im dwm.exe from an administrator prompt, or enable Restart dwm.exe when the mod is unloaded (the screen flickers briefly; apps stay open). Until then, a button can look wrong or be missing after the mod is turned off, for example the maximize button when the mod was turned on while a window was maximized and turned off before it was restored. dwm.exe is never restarted twice within 30 seconds, and the mod refuses to load if dwm.exe started 4 or more times within a minute.
  • The circles or custom images are global. Excluded apps keep them too; only their layout stays at the Windows default.
  • When the mod is turned on or off, or when a layout, exclusion, color or style setting changes, DWM is asked to refresh itself so that open windows get the new layout; no window is resized. Changing the debug log does not trigger a refresh.
  • The mod hooks internal, undocumented functions of uDWM.dll. A Windows update can change them and stop the mod until it is updated.
  • If you report a bug, turn on Write debug log and attach the Windhawk log output.

Compatibility and known issues

  • Apps that draw their own title bar (Office apps, Chrome, Edge and others) cannot be changed by this mod. The Titlebar For Everyone mod by Ingan121 can make them use the standard title bar.
  • At 125% and 150% display scaling, the maximize circle can show the wrong color (known issue).
